title: Every company should have a Brain — Garry Tan, Y Combinator
talk_summary: Garry Tan argues the leverage in AI-native companies is not the model but how work is wired: skill files as employees, resolver tables as org charts, and a curated 'company brain' that decides which context an agent loads. He stresses separating latent-space work (judgment, vague intent) from deterministic-space work (state, computation) and never doing one-off work without skillifying it.

takeaways.what_they_do: After an agent produces a good result, they convert the successful procedure into a reusable skill file loaded into the harness, so the same request never has to be re-derived.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have to ask for something twice, you failed

takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly decide which computation lives in the LLM (taste, judgment, vague intent) versus in deterministic code (state, arrays, seating math), keeping deterministic state out of the context window.

takeaways.technique: Curated company brain with provenance and contradiction checks
takeaways.what_they_do: A retrieval layer ('library plus librarian') decides which few documents load per task; every fact carries provenance, contradictions are checked, and a human+agent librarian prunes stale entries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Retrieval will surface a stale fact with total confidence

takeaways.what_they_do: A resolver table maps incoming task types to the skill/agent that handles them, functioning as the org chart that routes work deterministically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A task comes in and the resolver decides who handles it and where it goes

takeaways.what_they_do: They write tests that assert the right skill file actually loads for a given task type, treating routing/loading correctness as a measurable eval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: having a test that says, 'When I need to alter a test file, does test.md actually get loaded?'

takeaways.technique: Encode review procedure as a maintained skill
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat review/process knowledge as skill files maintained by engineers, so the procedure is explicit and versioned rather than implicit in prompts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they hire engineers whose job it is to maintain those skills
